ai.description: This slender, nocturnal snake reaches 1.2 meters. It is brown with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a distinctive dark stripe behind each eye. The head is broad and distinct from the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga gocool* is best distinguished by its lack of a dark postocular stripe, a feature present in nearly all other Indian *Boiga* species, resulting in a plain-sided head.
ai.habitat: The Eastern Cat Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in low-to-mid altitude hilly terrain and dense vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Eastern Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively prowling through trees and shrubs to hunt for small vertebrates like lizards and frogs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga gocool* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April to August) in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: Boiga gocool is found in Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting lowland forests and foothills at low elevations.
